sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: REVERSAL: The COMPLETE dependency contract deterministically requires the canonical hasDistressAlertDevice relationship, so the earlier instruction to omit it is no longer valid despite its potential overlap with the survival-craft distress path. Add hasDistressAlertDevice on its declared lifeboat owner, with the required range/cardinality semantics, while retaining the existing ship-owned relationships and the survival-craft device paths. Preserve the target restriction to survivalCraft nodes reached through hasSurvivalCraft and represented by the declared lifeboat relationships, conditioned on shipOperatesInLowAirTemperature=true and releasedRescueBoatOrLifeboat=true. Deterministic validation remains invalid until hasDistressAlertDevice is encoded.

Repair the semantic targeting and eliminate duplicate device obligations. The SPARQL target selects only lifeboat nodes, but survivalCraftHasLocationSignalDevice, survivalCraftHasOnSceneCommunicationDevice, and survivalCraftHasShipToShoreDistressAlertDevice each have requiredOwner survivalCraft; placing those properties on the selected lifeboat nodes violates their declared owners and the COMPLETE model path via hasSurvivalCraft. Construct a target/path that reaches survivalCraft nodes through the declared ship-to-survivalCraft relationship while restricting them to the released rescue boats and lifeboats represented by the declared lifeboat relationships and release applicability. Do not additionally require hasDistressAlertDevice as a separate distress-device obligation when the survival-craft ship-to-shore distress path already encodes that same requirement, because the current graph can require two distinct distress devices and is not a faithful minimum-count check. Retain all required ship-owned relationships, including hasLifeboat, hasOtherSurvivalCraft, hasRequiredRescueBoatOrLifeboat, and hasSurvivalCraft, without relocating component properties to the ship.

Repair the semantic targeting while preserving the prior instruction: remove the separate hasDistressAlertDevice obligation, which duplicates the distress requirement and can require two distinct devices. Retain the required ship-owned relationships, including hasLifeboat, hasOtherSurvivalCraft, hasRequiredRescueBoatOrLifeboat, and hasSurvivalCraft, but enforce the three device minimums only on survivalCraft nodes reached through hasSurvivalCraft that correspond to the released rescue boats or lifeboats represented by the declared lifeboat relationships. Do not relocate survival-craft device properties to lifeboats or the ship.
